content.comment_body: No. For a [product_name] standard module, you need at least [product_name] [version_no]. For another version of the [product_name], you need at least [product_name] [version_no]. The latest hardware requires at least [product_name] [version_no]. If you own a complete license for [product_name] [version_no], you can upgrade to the current [product_name] [version_no] for free. The upgrade is available for download on the official website: [document] After downloading, make sure to run the setup with administrator privileges.

analysis.insight_summary: The core issue is confusion over software and hardware compatibility, particularly users trying to use outdated [product_name] software with new hardware modules. Guidance is provided for upgrading, including a free upgrade path for licensed users, but this information is only found after users seek clarification.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the latest hardware to be compatible with older versions of [product_name] software or to receive clear upgrade instructions if compatibility is not available.
